title: On-Demand Fidelity Orchestrator — product brief and go-to-market playbook
author: Priya Menon
body:
Overview:

The On-Demand Fidelity Orchestrator (ODO) is a product initiative to provide per-request fidelity selection and short-lived scaling of inference resources based on predictive request signals, business rules, and customer-specified SLOs. ODO enables customers to get the latency and cost benefits of lower-fidelity variants for routine requests while preserving high-fidelity outputs for requests that materially affect product quality or revenue. This doc summarizes the product concept, success metrics, technical requirements, rollout phases, and go-to-market (GTM) packaging recommendations.

Goals:
- Reduce aggregate per-token cost for transactional workloads by 20–40% for participating tenants without increasing user-visible errors.
- Preserve fidelity for high-impact requests (as defined by customers) with >= 99% fidelity-hit rate for flagged requests.
- Provide transparent billing and audit trails showing fidelity decisions and economic impact.

Non-Goals:
- This is not a model compression program (we do not change model weights).
- ODO will not replace existing dedicated capacity or private deployment SLAs; features will be opt-in and manifest as routing/policy layers.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineers (integrate SDKs and routing policies).
- Product owners (define request-level fidelity signals and acceptance criteria).
- Finance and procurement (evaluate cost regression and crediting).
- SRE/ops (monitor SLOs, capacity, and rollback).

Key user scenarios:
1) e‑commerce chat: non-transactional browsing questions can be served at medium fidelity; purchase confirmations and policy questions get high fidelity.
2) Summarization: background summarization uses quantized variants, while legal-sensitive pages are escalated to full-fidelity models.
3) A/B experiments: product teams run fidelity-aware experiments to trade cost vs. conversion lift.

Product requirements (functional):
1. Policy engine: support declarative rules (by route, user tier, endpoint, or signal probability) and an engine to evaluate per-request routing. Accepted example rule syntax: "route == '/checkout' and confidence(user_intent) > 0.8 -> fidelity: high".
2. Predictive signal model: a lightweight classifier that emits a "fidelity_score" (0.0–1.0) with a 100ms max latency budget; model served in the edge tier or as a pre-routing hook.
3. Per-request routing: dynamic routing to model variants (high/medium/low) or local cache fast-paths. Must respect pinned tenants and explicit customer overrides.
4. Telemetry: emit odo.fidelity_decision, odo.fidelity_score, odo.latency_delta_ms, odo.cost_multiplier, and route-level counters. Must be wire-compatible with existing telemetry schema.
5. Auditing and explainability: store last 30 days of fidelity decisions per-tenant with reason and score for billing and dispute resolution.
6. SDK/API: expose flags in Redwood SDKs and REST API to annotate requests (e.g., priority_hint, business_impact).
7. Rollback/fallback: automatic fallback to nearest compatible variant on model mismatch or capacity shortage; configurable SLO thresholds for fallback.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- Latency impact: median added routing latency <= 15ms for hosted API; 95th percentile <= 50ms.
- Reliability: fidelity decision subsystem SLO 99.9% availability.
- Cost reporting accuracy: end-to-end billing attribution error < 0.5% for monthly reports.
- Security: fidelity decision logs must be scrubbed of PII and respect customer confidentiality settings.

Telemetry and observability (table):
| Metric | Description | Target | Owner |
| odo.fidelity_decisions.count | # of decisions by fidelity tier | N/A | platform-telemetry |
| odo.fidelity_score.distribution | Distribution of predictive scores | track drift monthly | applied-ml |
| odo.latency_delta_ms.p50/p95 | Added latency from ODO | p50 <= 15ms, p95 <=50ms | eng-runtime |
| odo.impact.cost_savings | Estimated cost savings attributed to ODO | > 20% for cohort | finance |

Success metrics (first 6 months):
- Participation: >= 30% of active paid tenants opt-in to ODO beta.
- Cost savings: average cohort-level token cost reduction >= 18%.
- Quality: measured customer-facing quality regressions <= 1% of requests (by automated evals and prompt sets).
- Revenue impact: no negative conversion delta in prioritized merchant cohort.

Pricing & packaging recommendations:
- Opt-in beta (no charge): during pilot phase, ODO decisions are free and cost savings are passed to customers; collect usage/telemetry.
- Consumption-offset model (GA): bill at standard token rates; provide an optional "odo-credit" add-on that guarantees X% of savings as credits if customer meets fidelity SLAs.
- Enterprise SKU: per-tenant configuration, dedicated telemetry retention, SLA-backed fidelity-decisions availability.
- Marketplace/partner model: integrate with channel partners to provide ODO as an upsell with pre-configured rule templates for common verticals (e.g., finance, healthcare).

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: Quality regressions for high-impact requests. Mitigations: conservative default policies (favor high fidelity), mandatory canary windows, automated fallback thresholds, and per-tenant guardrails.
- Risk: Billing disputes due to opaque decisions. Mitigations: detailed per-request audit logs, a billing reconciliation API, and refund crediting playbook.
- Risk: Added latency hurts low-latency SLAs. Mitigations: inline classifier optimization, routing bypass for pinned low-latency routes, regional edge placement.

Implementation notes and contracts for engineering teams:
- Runtime changes: eng-serving-runtime to implement an async policy-eval hook that returns routing directives with max latency 50ms. Contract: JSON response {decision: string, reason: string, score: float, cost_multiplier: float}. (Note: this JSON contract is illustrative; finalize in runtime API spec).
- ML requirements: applied-ml will provide the first predictive fidelity classifier; initial model must be <2MB and serveable from edge caches.
- Observability: eng-platform to add odo.* metrics to per-route dashboards and to wire alerts for fidelity errors > 0.5% in 5m windows.
- SDK updates: eng-developer-experience to add request annotations (priority_hint, business_impact) and a toggle for client-side prediction override.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Internal alpha (Q4 2026): enable on staging, instrument telemetry, run synthetic traffic experiments. Owners: applied-ml + eng-runtime.
2) Private beta (Q1 2027): 10 enterprise customers; weekly check-ins and billing reconciliation; collect GTM assets. Owners: product + customer-success + growth.
3) Public beta (Q2 2027): self-serve opt-in for hosted tenants; add SDK docs and example recipes. Owners: devx + docs.
4) GA (Q3 2027): enterprise packaging, billing integration, and marketplace listing. Owners: product + sales + finance.

Canary & experiment playbook (steps):
1. Create per-tenant rule with 5% traffic in ODO path.
2. Monitor automated quality evals and user metrics for 24–72 hours.
3. If quality regressions < 0.5% and latency within targets, increase traffic to 25% for 7 days.
4. Certify tenant for full rollout when both quality and cost savings targets are met and finance signs off.

GA readiness checklist (must pass all):
- Telemetry coverage: all odo.* metrics present and dashboards in product-console.
- Billing: reconciliation API and monthly report validated with finance.
- Security: PII scrubbers and access controls reviewed by security.
- SLOs: fidelity decision availability >= 99.9% in last 30 days.
- Docs & SDKs: integration guides, sample rules, and migration notes published.

Customer-facing release notes (example):
- Feature: On-Demand Fidelity Orchestrator (ODO) — opt-in fidelity routing to reduce inference cost while preserving quality for high-impact requests.
- Beta availability: self-serve from Q2 2027; enterprise packaging in Q3 2027.
- How to try: enable via Console -> Routes -> Fidelity rules or set priority_hint in SDK.

Open questions (short):
- What default fidelity thresholds should apply for self-serve customers?
- Should ODO decisions be included in per-token billing lines, or as a separate crediting line?
- Will private deployments include the predictive classifier, or require customers to host their own?

Appendix: example default fidelity tiers and expected cost multipliers
| Tier | Description | Typical use | Cost multiplier | Expected latency impact |
| high | Full model variant (no quantization) | Transactional or high-stakes requests | 1.0x | +0–5ms routing |
| medium | Quantized / trimmed variant with partial KV caching | General conversational traffic | 0.65x | +5–20ms |
| low | Aggressive quantization, prefetched context | Background tasks and non-critical replies | 0.45x | +10–35ms |
